translationRepairs: On arriving, Mian sent the general Li Guan and Rongzhou prefect Wang Hongren to campaign together against them. All were executed and the Five Ridges were pacified.
On arriving, Mian sent the general Li Guan and Rongzhou prefect Wang Hong to campaign together against them. All were executed and the Five Ridges were pacified.
Chinese has 王翃; the following 人 means jointly/with others, not part of the personal name. Idiomatic wrongly fuses it as Wang Hongren.
Li Gao, styled Zilan, was a great-great-grandson of Prince of Cao Ming, a descendant of the succession prince Zhan.
Li Gao, styled Zilan, was a great-great-grandson of Prince of Cao Ming, and son of the succession prince Zhan.
Chinese 嗣王戢之子 means son of succession prince Zhan, not a vague descendant.
His father Ze Yan held the posts of prefect over Han, Bao, Xiang, and Qi and bore the title Duke of Ande; wherever he served, he was known for stern efficiency.
His father Zeyan held the posts of prefect over Han, Bao, Xiang, and Qi and bore the title Duke of Ande; wherever he served, he was known for stern efficiency.
擇言 is a single given name; spacing as Ze Yan obscures that it is one personal name.
Xianzong took elixirs in excess and suddenly developed a disorder of frenzy and agitation, until he abandoned the throne.
Xianzong took elixirs in excess and suddenly developed a disorder of frenzy and agitation, until he passed away.
棄代 is an imperial death euphemism ('left the age'), not abdication or abandoning the throne; the idiomatic rendering correctly has death.
Muzong, while in the Eastern Palace, wrung his hands over this affair; when he assumed mourning, he banished and executed them all.
Muzong, while in the Eastern Palace, wrung his hands over this affair; when he observed mourning [on taking the throne], he banished and executed them all.
及居喪 marks mourning at succession after Xianzong's death, not merely assuming mourning as an isolated act; the idiomatic version captures the throne-in-mourning sense.
